summary: CheckYourself audited the public GitHub repo after the CLI/MCP release. The final pass fixed the package-script redaction review comment, added support/security triage, proved all 20 coverage surfaces, and reached 100/100 with no open findings.

language_mode.reason: The product determines candidate second-language support at run time and asks before using it.

coverage.evidence: README, START_HERE, and bootstrap define audience, outputs, and approval workflow.
CLI describe, manifest, and docs define the file-first architecture.
Dashboard template, smoke check, rendered dashboard, and screenshot exist.
No hosted backend, upload endpoint, or webhook receiver.
No auth, account, role, session, or admin runtime.
No database, migrations, or persisted user records.
No multitenant runtime or user data boundary.
Gitleaks passed; package scripts redact secrets; private Creator Kit is ignored.
SECURITY.md exists; secret-redaction tests cover JSON and Markdown output.
Local-first, no telemetry, and docs warn against sharing sensitive data.
10 unit tests, schema validation, py_compile, gitleaks, and MCP smoke pass.
GitHub Actions validates public shape, CLI contracts, MCP wrapper, tests, and gitleaks.
Public GitHub repo is live; git history is rollback for static repo changes.
No cloud runtime or IaC ships in the public product.
Progressive context loading and dashboard opt-in are documented.
No service workload; context-size control is documented.
SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, issue template, and Actions logs define triage surfaces.
Static open-source repo; recovery is GitHub history, cloneability, and future releases.
AGENTS, rules, coverage matrix, scoring method, schemas, and fixture govern behavior.
Learning templates, output, changelog, and dogfood reports tie findings to learning.

findings.title: Package scripts could leak credential-shaped values into generated output
findings.plain_risk: A user could hand an AI generated context that still contains a token embedded in a package script.
findings.next_step: Keep the redaction regression test in the CLI suite.

findings.title: Maintainer support/security triage was not documented
findings.plain_risk: Users would not know where to report bugs, security issues, or stale examples.
findings.next_step: Use GitHub Issues and security handling docs for incoming reports.

findings.title: Dogfood artifacts reflected the old 92 score
findings.plain_risk: Public proof would look stale after the CLI/MCP release.
findings.next_step: Refresh dogfood proof after future major interface changes.

next_approval: No approval batch remains. The final dogfood pass is complete.

learning_priorities.concept: Redact generated output, not just findings
learning_priorities.plain_english: A tool can detect a secret and still leak it somewhere else. Every generated output path needs redaction.
learning_priorities.why: The PR review comment found that package scripts could echo secret-bearing commands into context files.
learning_priorities.do_this_next: When adding a new output field, ask whether it could contain credentials and add a regression test.
learning_priorities.success_signal: The test suite proves a fake token never appears in JSON or Markdown output.
learning_priorities.source_title: GitHub Docs: Removing sensitive data from a repository
learning_priorities.why_this_source_is_trusted: GitHub maintains the official guidance for repository secret exposure.

learning_priorities.plain_english: A clean scan is not the same as a complete audit. The score reaches 100 only when coverage proves the relevant surfaces.
learning_priorities.why: The CLI correctly capped confidence when coverage was missing.
learning_priorities.do_this_next: Pair every final score with a coverage file and a command that reproduces the score.
learning_priorities.success_signal: The score command returns 100/high with no caps and a complete coverage check.
learning_priorities.why_this_source_is_trusted: This is the repository's canonical scoring contract.
learning_priorities.youtube_title: Evals in Action: From Frontier Research to Production Applications
learning_priorities.video_trust_note: Official OpenAI channel; useful framing for evidence-based AI evaluation.
